subject: Integration preflight: connector stability, retries, and rate fallback
body:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@edgeapps.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: dev@edgeapps.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood onboarding — preflight items and stability questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profiles. Before we lock the kickoff date we need a short preflight checklist from Redwood that covers: SDK setup, migration from our existing /v1/text endpoint to your streaming endpoint, recommended retry & timeout settings, and how to handle rate-limit throttling during our first 48h of traffic.

Can you send a concise plan (including any sample curl/snippet we can run in our staging env)? We will share the network diagram (attached) and schedule procurement signatures after the kickoff date is set.

Best,
Maria Gonzalez\Head of Integrations, EdgeApps

--
Attachment: network-architecture.png (image/png)

------------------------------------------------------------

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@edgeapps.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding — preflight items and stability questions

Thanks Maria — quick plan below. Attaching a one-pager action plan and a minimal SDK patch you can drop into your staging repo.

High-level preflight (aim for a 2-3 day warmup window):
1) SDK setup and smoke tests (Day 0)
   - Drop sdk-connection-sample.patch into your staging repo (attached). Patch contains minimal client init and example request.
   - Smoke test: run 'make smoke' which executes 5 short generation calls (<= 64 tokens) against our staging endpoint. Expect <120ms p50 on our staging GPU pool.

2) Endpoint migration (Day 1)
   - Current: POST https://api.edgeapps.com/v1/text -> returns sync JSON
   - New: POST https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-small&api_key=XXX (supports chunked streaming and SSE)
   - Migration strategy: dual-write for 24h (send identical payloads to both endpoints, compare outputs via checksum and a small diff-matcher). If checksum mismatch > 0.5% across 100 sampled requests, pause rollout and log examples to the shared drive.

3) Retries and timeouts (recommended):
   - Client-side socket timeout: 30s
   - Connect timeout: 3s
   - Per-request deadline: 45s (fail fast after deadline)
   - Retries: idempotent-only path (embeddings/rerank) use 3 retries with exponential backoff starting at 200ms, factor 2, jitter 100ms. For non-idempotent generation calls, limit to 1 retry and only after explicit user action.

Example backoff pseudo-config (in your client):
{
  "max_retries": 3,
  "initial_backoff_ms": 200,
  "backoff_factor": 2.0,
  "max_backoff_ms": 5000,
  "jitter_ms": 100
}

4) Rate-limit handling & warmup (first 48h):
   - Implement a 30-minute warming ramp (start at 10% traffic, 25% at T+15m, 50% at T+60m, 100% at T+3h) for critical endpoints.
   - Client-side behavior on 429: respect Retry-After header if present; otherwise apply exponential backoff starting 500ms. Do not retry more than 4 times for a single user request.
   - SLO safeguard: set a per-user concurrency limit (default 3) to protect downstream tokens.

5) Observability & alerting (ops):
   - Add tracing header x-redwood-trace to correlate requests.
   - Log token usage and 429/5xx responses to the shared drive (we provided a HubSpot ingest link).

Quick sample (curl -> streaming):
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small","prompt":"Summarize: ...","max_tokens":64}' \
  https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/stream

Minimal client snippet (nodejs):
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const controller = new AbortController();
const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 45000); // per-request deadline
try {
  const res = await fetch('https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/stream', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + process.env.RW_KEY, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-small', prompt: 'Hello' }),
    signal: controller.signal
  });
  // stream handling omitted for brevity
} finally { clearTimeout(timeout); }

Attachments: edgeapps-onboard-action-plan.xlsx, sdk-connection-sample.patch

Thanks — next steps: if this looks good I suggest a kickoff Tuesday 2026-09-28 where Monica will run the onboarding and Laura will own the code review cadence.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra\Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

--

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@edgeapps.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: dev@edgeapps.com
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding — preflight items and stability questions

Rishi — this is great and very actionable. A couple quick clarifications from our dev lead:
1) Our current client retries are centralized in a middleware. Is it safe to apply the backoff config there or do you require per-call instrumentation?
2) For the checksum sampling, do you have a small script we can run to compute the diffs you mentioned?

We can attach procurement signatures the day after kickoff. Sending the network diagram to your team separately.

Thanks,
Maria

Maria — assigning as discussed. Monica here (CSM) — I'll run the kickoff and own the runbook during the warmup window. Sequence I plan:
- Day -1: Provision staging keys and run the smoke test (Rishi's patch).
- Day 0: Dual-write migration and checksum sampling (Monica + Edge devs).
- Day 1: Scale ramp, monitor 429s and error budget.

Answers to your questions:
1) Backoff config: central middleware is fine. We'll recommend you add per-call metadata (x-redwood-trace) but not required for backoff to work.
2) Checksum script: attached 'checksum-sample.sh' inside the action-plan xlsx (tab 'helpers'). We'll also drop a small python helper into the shared drive after this email.

I will schedule a 45-minute kickoff with the EdgeApps dev/ops team for 2026-09-28 10:00 PDT. Please confirm availability.

Thanks,
Monica Patel\Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@edgeapps.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding — preflight items and stability questions

Looping in ops-run escalation notes and the SLA exception process (short):
- If warmup sees >5% sustained 5xxs over 10m, auto-roll back traffic to redwood-legacy pool and notify the on-call.
- For rate-related degradation, we can temporarily increase burst capacity for this customer (requires approval). Rishi — can you flag the request in HubSpot after procurement signs?

Also adding a quick checklist for the implementation team to avoid common mistakes:
- Ensure TLS inspection is disabled on the gateway for streaming endpoints (it breaks chunked responses).
- Do not shorten the client-side per-request deadline below 30s for streaming flows — causes partial token truncation.
- Validate that the middleware preserves x-request-id from your API gateway; we rely on that for correlating logs.

Thanks — Vivek
Director, Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference

--

- Rishi: finalize kickoff invite and attach signed SOW link to HubSpot (DEAL-4821).
